placement.claim: Each long-running role workflow owns its resume-critical semantic projection over the shared opaque durable-state primitive. The control plane owns logical identity and role routing, activation, runtime-binding registration, coordination, delivery, subscriptions, reconciliation, and bounded projections without owning workflow meaning or agent-state consequences. Parent/child topology representation, visibility-policy enforcement, and physical adapter placement remain provisional.

reopening_conditions: Implemented control-plane evidence contradicts the named product-direction ownership of logical identity, routing, activation, runtime binding, coordination, delivery, subscriptions, reconciliation, or bounded projections.
Parent/child topology, visibility-policy enforcement, or lifecycle-query consumers require a different boundary from the provisional agent-state and control-plane split.
A role recovery vertical cannot reconstruct correctly from a role-owned projection plus references to stronger domain artifacts.
The current snapshot cannot be explained from predecessor-linked semantic consequences without relying on provider transcripts, Git reflogs, or model recollection.
Observed multi-writer, topology-query, authorization, or cleanup requirements cannot be supported truthfully by the current Git-ref durable-state adapter.
Independent-review recovery shows that preserving findings outside the provider session compromises the required independence boundary.
Dogfooding shows that one proposed role profile duplicates stronger packet, receipt, checkpoint, schedule, or repository state rather than referencing it.

authority.decision_owner: user or future explicitly authorized architecture owner

relationships.rationale: Proposal packets own durable candidate and decision context, while this proposal owns only unfinished live operational position and references packet state rather than duplicating it.
